title: [replay] perf(record): start recording instantly — preloaded overlays and shade, devices acquired during the countdown
body:
> **Replay of [niway-dev/kaipu-record#402](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/402)** for the code-review benchmark. Base `a25424d`, head `01dfe73`: the same commits the original reviewers saw, so the diff is byte-identical. Never merged. Method and scoring: [wachiman/docs/benchmark](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman/tree/main/docs/benchmark). The original description follows.

---

## Summary

Recording felt slow to start. The owner's `[record-timing]` log (`bun run dev`, 3 displays) showed three waits the user sits through:

| Step | Before | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Click → capture overlay visible | 1.06–1.24 s (2.5 s cold; 0.36 s when preloaded windows matched) | Preloaded overlay "spares" were keyed on the frame display (cursor position at warm time), mode and intent, so with several displays they rarely matched and every pick loaded fresh renderers. |
| Pick → 3-2-1 visible | ~0.51 s | The shade window loaded a new renderer each take; the countdown waits for it (#391). |
| Countdown end → timer runs | ~1.03 s ("Starting…") | Screen, mic and encoder were acquired only when the countdown reached 0. |

This PR removes all three:

1. **Acquire during the countdown** (17b45df1, fde4e1a7). The engine is split into `prepareEngine` (screen, mic, compositor, audio mix, encoder) and `begin()` (starts the output). The take is acquired while 3-2-1 runs; at 0 the input is resolved again and, if unchanged, `begin()` starts at once. Countdown frames never reach the file: the output starts at 0, and with `synced-zero` the first frame after `begin()` is time 0. If the input changed during the countdown (source, area, mic, system audio, quality, watermark), the early acquisition is released and the take acquires again. Cancel releases everything acquired (tracks, compositor, audio context, session file, cursor track). From the Record page the main window is hidden through a new `recording:hide-main-window` invoke and the take waits 50 ms (an estimate) for it to leave the screen before encoding. Countdown off: unchanged.
2. **Overlay spares reused on every pick** (11020663). The spare key is now only what truly needs a reload: display set, geometry, scale (plus locale/theme). Mode, intent and frame display are sent as state before the window is shown; a spare paints nothing until its first state.
3. **Countdown shade preloaded** (11020663). One hidden, neutral shade window is loaded after launch and reused: `show` moves it and sends region + phase as state; `hide` keeps it and resets it to neutral so a reused window never repaints the previous take.

## Merged with #399 (mic audio settings)

01dfe73f merges main after #399 landed. Everything #399 builds at start (mic analyser, level/mute gains, system volume, duck/mute gains, mix analyser, late-mic and noise-reopen paths) is now built in `prepareEngine`; `begin()` keeps what needs the output (`output.start`, `firstMediaTimestamp`, thumbnail, ducking loop). Live audio controls are one `LiveAudioControls` object shared by the prepared engine and the handle, so a setting changed during the 3-2-1 reaches the take. `release()` before `begin` tears down the whole audio graph.

The input-changed check (`needsNewAcquisition`) re-acquires only for source, area, quality, watermark, or another mic device; mic on/off, system audio on/off and #399's audio settings are applied to the prepared engine instead (keeping system audio in would re-acquire every take on a macOS dev build, where the toggle is written back to off without a loopback track).

Known gaps, same as on main and #399 alone: a mic/system toggle in the short "starting" gap before the settings forwarder attaches can be missed; a mic switched while muted during the countdown stays on the first device (muted), matching #399's no-switch-mid-take rule.

## Objective and what is measured

Objective (owner, 2026-10-27): overlay visible ≤300 ms after the click; countdown visible ≤100 ms after the pick; timer running ≤150 ms after the countdown ends — **on a packaged build**. Nothing here was measured in a running app yet: the numbers above come from the owner's dev-mode log, and the gains are argued from the code and unit tests. New `[record-timing]` marks make the check a log read: `overlay spares reused` / `overlay loaded fresh`, `countdown shade reused` / `countdown shade loaded fresh`, `acquiring during countdown`, `acquired during countdown`, `countdown ended`, `input changed during countdown, acquiring again`, `clock started at countdown end +Nms`.

## Risks to check by hand

- **First frame of a Record-page take**: the 50 ms wait for the main window to hide is an estimate. The video's first frame must not show the Kaipu window.
- **Shade across displays with different scale factors**: the same window now moves with `setBounds`; check the first frame on a Retina ↔ non-Retina move.
- **mediabunny pause semantics**: starting the output paused was rejected after reading mediabunny 1.61.4 (a source paused before its first frame breaks the sampler's time base); not run.
- **macOS indicators**: the mic/screen indicator now turns on when the countdown starts, and must turn off at once on cancel.

## Verification

- `bun run verify` on the combined branch: exit 0 — workflow checks, lint (0 errors), `oxfmt --check`, build, `check-types`, tests (12/12 Turbo tasks; kaipu-record 287 files, 2683 tests). After the #399 merge (01dfe73f): `bun run verify` exit 0, kaipu-record 298 files, 2822 tests.
- New tests: engine prepare/begin/release (6, failed first: `prepareEngine is not a function`), store acquire-during-countdown (7), hub hide-main-window handler (1), overlay spares reuse (cursor elsewhere, mode/intent switch, state before show, reload on display change), shade reuse and reset (new `recording-shade-window.test.ts`). The overlay/shade tests were written first but not run against the old code.
- E2E not run locally (CI runs it).

## How to test it yourself

`bun run dev` with several displays; Settings → Recording → Countdown 3 s. Wait ~5 s after launch (the spares and the shade preload).

1. **Overlay:** put the mouse on a different display from the last frame, click Start recording (Frame). The overlay appears at once on every display. Terminal: `overlay spares reused`, then `overlay shown on display N` within ~300 ms of `start clicked`. Before: `overlay shown` at +1.0–1.2 s.
2. **Switch modes** inside the overlay (Frame ↔ Screen): no reload.
3. **Countdown:** pick an area. The 3-2-1 appears at once: `countdown shade reused`, and `countdown shade shown` ≤100 ms after `renderer: requestStartRecording`. Before: ~510 ms.
4. **Timer:** when "1" ends the timer starts right away, with no "Starting…": `clock started at countdown end +Nms` with N ≤150. Before: ~1.03 s.
5. **Record page:** start from the Record page with the app visible; after stopping, check the first frame of the video does not show the Kaipu window.
6. **Cancel:** start a countdown and press Esc during 3-2-1. The macOS mic/screen indicator turns off at once.
7. **Second take** on another display or area: the shade never shows the previous area or border.
8. **Countdown Off:** same as before (bar shows "Starting…" while it acquires).
9. **Audio during the countdown (#399):** start a 3 s countdown, change the mic level or turn noise suppression on during 3-2-1; the recording uses the new setting from its first second.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Recording setup now begins during the countdown, with the latest capture settings applied when recording starts.
  * The app window hides at countdown end, and the recording indicator is ready to appear without loading from scratch.
  * Screenshot overlays can be prepared ahead of time and reused across capture modes when the display layout is unchanged.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Recording and screenshot overlays receive their current state before appearing, helping prevent outdated regions or modes from being shown.
